title: Atom Learning Model (ALM): how a real classroom got tokenised
abstract: arXiv:2608.21106v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The Atom Learning Model (ALM) tokenises a school curriculum. Two secondary mathematics textbooks were read by machine into 1,934 atoms, each one thing a learner can do in a single step, ordered by 4,616 machine-written prerequisite links. Both sides of a lesson are then expressed in that one structure: a question is a set of atoms plus everything beneath them, a child's ability is a score between 0 and 1 on every atom of the same graph, and whether a question suits a child is arithmetic over one index, with no difficulty parameter fitted for either side. Nobody wrote an atom, a link or a question. Reading the 757 pages cost {\pounds}55, building the whole structure cost between {\pounds}615 and {\pounds}1,230, and against it the system composed 6,648 questions for 373 children in two English secondary schools over seven weeks, at 26p per composed question. Four measurements went against expectation. The cost is in the links, not the pa

translated_title: 原子学习模型（ALM）：真实课堂如何被标记化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.21106v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：原子学习模型（ALM）将学校课程标记化。两本中学数学教科书被机器读取为1,934个原子，每个原子是学习者可以单步完成的一件事，并由4,616条机器编写的先决条件链接排序。课堂的两侧随后以这一结构表达：一个问题是一组原子及其下方所有内容，一个孩子的能力是对同一图中每个原子打分0到1之间的分数，而问题是否适合孩子是对一个索引的算术运算，无需为任何一侧拟合难度参数。没有人编写原子、链接或问题。阅读757页花费55英镑，构建整个结构花费615至1,230英镑，系统在七周内为两所英国中学的373名孩子组合了6,648个问题，每个组合问题成本26便士。四项测量结果与预期不符。成本在于链接，而非页面。
tldr: 该论文提出原子学习模型（ALM），通过自动标记化课程和生成先决链接，以极低成本为课堂动态组合个性化问题，无需人工编写或难度参数拟合。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Atom Learning Model (ALM), which tokenizes curricula and generates prerequisite links automatically, enabling low-cost dynamic composition of personalized questions without manual writing or difficulty fitting.
